Drew y=2cos x and both branches of y=cot x from their equations on [0,2pi] at 0.9pt (rules 9, 10). The asymptotes x=pi and x=2pi use the house aux dashes, not the paper's long dashes (rule 3). I put dots at the four computed intersections (rule 16). The two lens regions between pi/6 and 5pi/6 are flat grey `shade`, lighter than the paper's dark grey (rule 5). The x tick labels are stacked fractions pi/2, 3pi/2 (rule 23). They sit below-left of each tick as on the crop, which keeps 0, pi and 2pi off the dashed asymptotes. 3pi/2 is the exception: it sits lower, between the two curves crossing at that point, so it touches neither (rules 11, 24). The tick labels are larger than the crop's tiny ones so they can be read. The point labels are moved slightly so they don't touch the curves. Overlay below 0.85: the paper's darker shading and the different label sizes account for most of it. Also the y=cot x label sits about 0.6 units lower than on the crop and could be moved up to about y=-2.4; there were no rounds left to fix it. | 25 Nov label-overlap fix: 3pi/2 lowered into the gap between the two curves
